question.problem:
Consider the function $y=(3{x}^{2})^{x}.$ Its derivative is given by 

$$
{y}^{′}=(3{x}^{2})^{x}\cdot g(x).
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
question.worked_solution:
We have the function 

$$
y=(3{x}^{2})^{x}.
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡((3{x}^{2})^{x}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3{x}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x\operatorname{ln}⁡(3{x}^{2})) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =(x)^{′}\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡(3{x}^{2}))+(x)\cdot {(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3{x}^{2}))}^{′} \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡(3{x}^{2})+x\cdot (\frac{1}{3{x}^{2}}\cdot 6x) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3{x}^{2})+2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve for ${y}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3{x}^{2})+2)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y=(3{x}^{2})^{x}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =(3{x}^{2})^{x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(3{x}^{2})+2)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡(3{x}^{2})+2.$
